To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the cytoskeletal polarization of B16F10 cells adherent to microcontact-printed substrates is influenced by the shape and curvature at the perimeter, and that this influence is modulated by actomyosin dynamics.
cells respond to local curvature at their periphery by modulating their actin cytoskeleton and this response can be modulated by altering contractility.
curvature and shape of the adhesive substrate influence the assembly of the actin cytoskeleton and that the influence of shape is modulated by actomyosin activity.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of cell geometry in the regulation of cell polarity and cell shape, which is a key feature of cell migration.
the role of cell shape on cell polarization and motility in the context of the extracellular environment.
the role of cell shape and cell-substratum adhesions on cell polarization.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the cell is able to sense and respond to curvature in a manner that is independent of the overall shape of the adhesive surface.
the cytoskeletal response to curvature at the perimeter is dependent on cell contractility.
curvature is a key geometric cue that influences the assembly of the lamellipodia at the leading edge of migrating cells.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
curvature at the perimeter can influence the assembly of lamellar structures, such as lamellipodia, and can also influence the assembly of contractile structures, such as stress fibers.
curvature is a key geometric cue in determining cell polarity.
curvature at the perimeter influences cell polarity, and the effect of curvature on cell polarity can be modulated by actomyosin contraction.
The main takeaway from our work is that
curvature at the perimeter can be used to direct cell polarization in the presence of other geometric cues.
cells are able to integrate multiple geometric cues to modulate cytoskeletal polarization.
the cytoskeletal response to geometric cues is not simply a linear sum of the responses to each cue, but is also dependent on cell contractility.
